subject: Contributing your functions to Stan - resolving c++ linker issues (invoke function via pointer)

messages.author: a7de39e424b27378
messages.subject: Contributing your functions to Stan - resolving c++ linker issues (invoke function via pointer)
parts:
Hi everybody,

I am writing some c++ functions for Stan.
I have a low-level function (called 'breit_wigner', see code snippet below)
that is invoked by another function (called 'amplitude'). However,
if I try to create a pointer to 'breit_wigner' and invoke the pointer
in 'amplitude', I get a linker error.

I guess I have to perform some changes in Stan's makefile?
Sorry, I am not providing a simplified MWE, but I do not expect precise
instructions. However, I would greatly appreciate an opinion (or an educated
guess), which files and where do I have to change, or at which point
the reference to 'breit_wigner' gets lost...

Thanks in advance!
Best regards,
Arseniy Tsipenyuk.

---------------
Here are some details. My '.hpp' files are included in 'stan/lib/stan_math_2.7.0/stan/math.hpp',
and all the functions are properly exposed to Stan parser (via appropriate changes in 'function_signatures.h').

First, a snippet of the code that works (everything is linked and compiled correctly,
and I am able to run my Stan model):
"""
  template <typename T> 
  std::vector<typename boost::math::tools::promote_arg<T>::type>
  amplitude(const Eigen::Matrix<T, Eigen::Dynamic, 1>& y) {                    //  Just a function that calls 'breit_wigner'                 
    return breit_wigner<T,Ext,R>(y(0), y(1));
  };
"""

I make the following alteration:
"""
   template <typename T>
  std::vector<T> (*my_ptr) (const T&, const T&) = &breit_wigner<T,Ext,R>;      // Pointer to 'breit_wigner'

  template <typename T> 
  std::vector<typename boost::math::tools::promote_arg<T>::type>
  amplitude(const Eigen::Matrix<T, Eigen::Dynamic,1>& y) {
    return (*my_ptr<T>)(y(0), y(1));                                           // Function that calls pointer to 'breit_wigner'
  };
"""

and get the following linker error (I manually broke some lines to improve readability):
"""
--- Linking C++ model ---
clang++
-DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS
-I src -I stan/src -isystem stan/lib/stan_math_2.7.0 -isystem stan/lib/eigen_3.2.4 -isystem stan/lib/boost_1.58.0 -isystem stan/..
-Wall -pipe -DEIGEN_NO_DEBUG -Wno-unused-function -Wno-uninitialized -Wno-c++11-long-long    -O3
-o ___my_path_to_my_stan_model___/STAN_data_generator src/cmdstan/main.cpp
-include ___my_path_to_my_stan_model___/STAN_data_generator.hpp
/tmp/gu95lik/main-c35eaa.o: In function `std::vector<Eigen::Matrix<boost::math::tools::promote_arg<double>::type, -1, 1, 0, -1, 1>,
                                                                             std::allocator<Eigen::Matrix<boost::math::tools::promote_arg<double>::type, -1, 1, 0, -1, 1> > >
                                                           amplitude<double>(Eigen::Matrix<double, -1, 1, 0, -1, 1> const&)':

src/cmdstan/main.cpp:(.text._ZN8amplitudeIdEESt6vectorIN5Eigen6MatrixIN5boost4math5tools11promote_argIT_E4typeELin1ELi1ELi0ELin1ELi1EEESaISB_EERKNS3_IS8_Lin1ELi1ELi0ELin1ELi1EEE[_ZN8amplitudeIdEESt6vectorIN5Eigen6MatrixIN5boost4math5tools11promote_argIT_E4typeELin1ELi1ELi0ELin1ELi1EEESaISB_EERKNS3_IS8_Lin1ELi1ELi0ELin1ELi1EEE]+0x93): undefined reference to `my_ptr<double>'

/tmp/gu95lik/main-c35eaa.o: In function `std::vector<Eigen::Matrix<boost::math::tools::promote_arg<stan::math::var>::type, -1, 1, 0, -1, 1>, std::allocator<Eigen::Matrix<boost::math::tools::promote_arg<stan::math::var>::type, -1, 1, 0, -1, 1> > > amplitude<stan::math::var>(Eigen::Matrix<stan::math::var, -1, 1, 0, -1, 1> const&)':

src/cmdstan/main.cpp:
(.text._ZN8amplitudeIN4stan4math3varEEESt6vectorIN5Eigen6MatrixIN5boost4math5tools11promote_argIT_E4typeELin1ELi1ELi0ELin1ELi1EEESaISE_EERKNS6_ISB_Lin1ELi1ELi0ELin1ELi1EEE[_ZN8amplitudeIN4stan4math3varEEESt6vectorIN5Eigen6MatrixIN5boost4math5tools11promote_argIT_E4typeELin1ELi1ELi0ELin1ELi1EEESaISE_EERKNS6_ISB_Lin1ELi1ELi0ELin1ELi1EEE]+0xa4): undefined reference to `my_ptr<stan::math::var>'
clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)
make: *** [___my_path_to_my_stan_model___/STAN_data_generator] Error 1

"""
Any ideas? Thanks for reading so far, anyway!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Contributing your functions to Stan - resolving c++ linker issues (invoke function via pointer)
parts:
> On Aug 13, 2015, at 11:22 AM, Arseniy Tsipenyuk <arseniy....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi everybody,
>
> I am writing some c++ functions for Stan.
> I have a low-level function (called 'breit_wigner', see code snippet below)
> that is invoked by another function (called 'amplitude'). However,
> if I try to create a pointer to 'breit_wigner' and invoke the pointer
> in 'amplitude', I get a linker error.
>
> I guess I have to perform some changes in Stan's makefile?

Only if you need to link object files, which you hopefully won't
have to do.

Do you have the source to both breit_wigner() and amplitude()?

If you read to the end of the error message, you'll see this:
> undefined reference to `my_ptr<stan::math::var>'

which is telling you that the linker can't find the code for my_ptr<var>.

Where is my_ptr defined and is it implemented for autodiff vars?
If it's header only, you should just be able to include it. If not,
you'll need to instantiate it for stan::math::var and then you will
need to modify the makefile so that it'll link.
> Sorry, I am not providing a simplified MWE,

What's an MWE?

Arseniy.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Contributing your functions to Stan - resolving c++ linker issues (invoke function via pointer)
parts:
Hello again,

Thanks! I have resolved my issue. The problem lied within my templated pointer declaration.
Just for the future reference, here is a full example of the code that allows to reproduce the correct
solution. I have tested it on a 'clean' version of CmdStan-2.7.0 after performing the following steps.

1) Replace the file cmdstan-2.7.0/stan/src/stan/lang/function_signatures.h with the provided file.
(The file was changed as follows: the lines
"""
// MWE_DIR__MY_SQUARE_HPP functions
add("my_square", DOUBLE_T, DOUBLE_T);
add("my_square_ptr_wrapper", DOUBLE_T, DOUBLE_T);

"""
were added in the beginning of the file.)

2) Replace the file cmdstan-2.7.0/stan/lib/stan_math_2.7.0/stan/math.hpp with the provided file.
(The file was changed as follows: the lines
"""

//      lib stan cmdstan-2.7.0
#include <../../../mwe_dir/my_square.hpp>
"""
were added to the end of the file.)

3) Create the folder called 'mwe_dir' in the CmdStan-2.7.0 directory.
Copy the files 'my_square.hpp' and '*.stan' to this directory. The 
'*.stan' files can be compiled and seem to sample correctly 
(tested with clang-3.4, c++11).

Best regards,
Arseniy.

On Thursday, August 13, 2015 at 10:35:16 PM UTC+2, Bob Carpenter wrote:

> On Aug 13, 2015, at 11:22 AM, Arseniy Tsipenyuk <arseniy....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi everybody,
>
> I am writing some c++ functions for Stan.
> I have a low-level function (called 'breit_wigner', see code snippet below)
> that is invoked by another function (called 'amplitude'). However,
> if I try to create a pointer to 'breit_wigner' and invoke the pointer
> in 'amplitude', I get a linker error.
>
> I guess I have to perform some changes in Stan's makefile?

Only if you need to link object files, which you hopefully won't
have to do.

Do you have the source to both breit_wigner() and amplitude()?

If you read to the end of the error message, you'll see this:

> undefined reference to `my_ptr<stan::math::var>'


which is telling you that the linker can't find the code for my_ptr<var>.

Where is my_ptr defined and is it implemented for autodiff vars?
If it's header only, you should just be able to include it.  If not,
you'll need to instantiate it for stan::math::var and then you will
need to modify the makefile so that it'll link.

> Sorry, I am not providing a simplified MWE,

What's an MWE?

- Bob

messages.author: a7de39e424b27378
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Contributing your functions to Stan - resolving c++ linker issues (invoke function via pointer)
parts:
Hi Bob,

thanks, but this is merely a proof-of-concept for more generic class of 
functions suited to partial wave analysis (PWA) of heavy meson decay. 
It requires complex variables and various other components. 
(See, e.g., http://arxiv.org/abs/1406.6311, Chapter 13. Among others, multiple 
formulas similar to 13.2.2 and factors therein are necessary.) 

Initially, I started with Stan implementation of the aforementioned functions, 
however, the *.stan files quickly outgrew several hundred lines and became 
completely unreadable. Rather than writing in Stan, it seemed simpler to implement 
all the low-level pieces of the analysis in C++. Another reason to instantiate 
partial waves in C++ is versatility: it becomes easier to cross-check the results 
with existing PWA modules such as ComPWA, RootPWA, and others.

Returning back to the motivation of my question. Pointers seem to be quite
useful to gather various functions with the same input/output (complex-valued 
functions describing partial wave amplitudes) to one vector-valued function. 
(Just as a point of interest: the same linker problem I have encountered arises
when invoking virtual functions for some templated base class.)

Current version of the code and some documentation may be found at 
https://github.com/atsipenyuk/mdeca and partly on
https://github.com/atsipenyuk/stan_pwa (migration to the latter is in progress). 
Right now I am performing many changes in order to improve the overall 
quality and readability of the project. I will be glad to provide a link to the 
stable version when I get so far. 

Best regards,
Arseniy.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Contributing your functions to Stan - resolving c++ linker issues (invoke function via pointer)
parts:
> On Aug 18, 2015, at 11:15 AM, Arseniy Tsipenyuk <arseniy....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Bob,
>
> thanks, but this is merely a proof-of-concept for more generic class of
> functions suited to partial wave analysis (PWA) of heavy meson decay.
> It requires complex variables and various other components.
> (See, e.g., http://arxiv.org/abs/1406.6311, Chapter 13. Among others, multiple
> formulas similar to 13.2.2 and factors therein are necessary.)
That's what I figured --- thanks for confirming.

> Initially, I started with Stan implementation of the aforementioned functions,
> however, the *.stan files quickly outgrew several hundred lines and became
> completely unreadable. Rather than writing in Stan, it seemed simpler to implement
> all the low-level pieces of the analysis in C++. Another reason to instantiate
> partial waves in C++ is versatility: it becomes easier to cross-check the results
> with existing PWA modules such as ComPWA, RootPWA, and others.

Stan's not really set up for easy testing, which for me is a dealbreaker
for anything other than simple code. There's a way to unit test functions
in Stan through R, but not through any of the other interfaces I know of.

> Returning back to the motivation of my question. Pointers seem to be quite
> useful to gather various functions with the same input/output (complex-valued
> functions describing partial wave amplitudes) to one vector-valued function.
> (Just as a point of interest: the same linker problem I have encountered arises
> when invoking virtual functions for some templated base class.)

Functors are the idiomatic way to do the same thing in C++. There's
a very good description of this in both the Vandevoorde and Josuttis
book and the Alexandrescu C++ books. It's also the way to interface with
the standard <algorithm> library built into C++ and there's even more support
in C++11 for binding and more general lambda abstracts (allowing functional programming
idioms), but we haven't gotten there yet with Stan because Python and R support
is lagging.

> Current version of the code and some documentation may be found at
> https://github.com/atsipenyuk/mdeca and partly on
> https://github.com/atsipenyuk/stan_pwa (migration to the latter is in progress).
> Right now I am performing many changes in order to improve the overall
> quality and readability of the project. I will be glad to provide a link to the
> stable version when I get so far.

Thanks.

- Bob
